description: This plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number and accuracy for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with visible tick marks at $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and employs a linear scale with visible tick marks ranging from 60 to 80 at intervals of 5 units, though the plotted data and grid lines extend higher. All six methods are represented by solid lines that demonstrate a steady upward trend across the four plotted data points along the x-axis. The "Base" method, represented by a black line with circle markers, increases from approximately 65% at the start of the x-axis to roughly 82% at the end. The "FT" method, shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rises from about 67% to 85%. The "IKE" method, depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, increases from approximately 69% to 87%. The "MEMIT" method, represented by a purple line with pentagon markers, grows from about 71% to 89%. The "MEND" method, shown as a brown line with diamond markers, rises from roughly 72% to 91%. Finally, the "ROME" method, depicted by a green line with square markers, increases from approximately 76% at the lowest co-occurrence number to roughly 94% at the highest.
